body: The Ascendant is the degree of the ecliptic rising above the eastern horizon at the moment a chart is cast. It defines the first-house cusp in quadrant house systems and depends on a known birth time.

Placidus is a quadrant house system that divides the ecliptic by proportional semi-arc, so house cusps fall at unequal distances. It is one of several house-system conventions — a coordinate choice, not a physical structure.

Synastry is the practice of comparing two natal charts by examining the angular relationships formed between each chart's positions. It is an interpretive tradition, not a measurement of a relationship's outcome.

Retrograde describes the apparent westward motion of a planet against the stars, an effect of observing from a moving Earth. It is a perspective phenomenon and does not mean the planet reverses its orbit.

The Midheaven is the degree of the ecliptic crossing the local meridian above the horizon at the chart moment. It marks the tenth-house cusp in quadrant house systems and, like the Ascendant, depends on a known birth time.
